Fix what the output names. Move the tasks it touches to in_progress with UpdateTask while you work and to tested once their tests pass; leave the rest of the board as it is.

Reproduce the failure with a run narrowed to the test the output names, fix it, then run that test again and build its project. The whole sweep runs again as soon as you stop with every task tested, so stopping on a fix you have not run costs another one.

CodeOutline on the failing test's file gives the line each test starts on: Read that test's range rather than the whole file.

The tasks the failure names:

Writing a file another hand changed [tested] (Stale write refused, Own writes are seeing, Folded read is not seeing, Unread file refused, A new file needs no read, No read-before-edit instruction, Who changed it): Every session that writes — plan, implement, cleanup, chat — is held to the same check, which the extension performs rather than the prompt asking for it.
files: src/extension.ts, src/agent/phases/implement.ts, src/agent/session/file-hands.ts, src/agent/session/stale-write-guard.ts, test/stale-write-guard.test.ts, test/implement.test.ts
proves: Stale write refused → test/stale-write-guard.test.ts StaleWriteGuard > stale_write_refused_when_the_file_changed_on_disk_since_it_was_read, Own writes are seeing → test/stale-write-guard.test.ts StaleWriteGuard > own_writes_are_seeing_so_two_edits_in_a_row_are_never_refused, Folded read is not seeing → test/tools.test.ts ReadTracker > forgetting_all_but_the_named_files_sends_the_rest_back_to_be_read, Unread file refused → test/stale-write-guard.test.ts StaleWriteGuard > unread_file_refused, A new file needs no read → test/stale-write-guard.test.ts StaleWriteGuard > a_new_file_needs_no_read, No read-before-edit instruction → test/implement.test.ts implement phase > no_read_before_edit_instruction_since_the_stale_write_guard_enforces_it, Who changed it → test/stale-write-guard.test.ts StaleWriteGuard > who_changed_it_names_the_other_kiwiagent_session_and_its_feature
note: "Who changed it" and the docs it cites (docs/features/coordination.md#Claims, docs/intent/agent.md) describe a fuller future "Claims" registry — deadlines, heartbeats, denying a live session's hold. This task's 7 rules only need naming who last wrote a file, so FileHands is deliberately a thin attribution log (one JSON file per session, path -> mtimeMs) rather than that fuller registry; a later task can extend the same .agent/sessions/*.json files rather than replace them. Left the existing inline staleness checks in openai-session/tools/write.ts and edit.ts untouched: they remain the own-loop engine's authoritative, unmodified behaviour, and StaleWriteGuard is an independent layer added at the hook level so it also reaches the Claude engine's native Edit/Write, which the inline checks never could. Mid-task the user confirmed (interrupt: "other agents might use other files, so postponing isnt good") that this hook-level approach, reaching the Claude engine now rather than deferring it, was the right choice — this settles where the check lives for the rest of the feature, so no further AskUser was needed on it.
built: StaleWriteGuard (src/agent/session/stale-write-guard.ts) implements SessionHooks with its own ReadTracker; added once, unconditionally, in setupFor()'s composeHooks(...) in src/extension.ts, so it holds every session — every mode, both the openai-compatible loop and the Claude SDK's native Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit — to the same read-before-write/stale-write check via the shared preToolUse/postToolUse hook pair. FileHands (src/agent/session/file-hands.ts) exports recordWrite(path, mtimeMs), whoWrote(path, mtimeMs): Promise<Hand | undefined>, and describeHand(hand): string; it persists one JSON registry per session under .agent/sessions/<sessionId>.json (path -> mtimeMs, plus the session's mode and feature), so any session — any process, any window — can attribute a file's current mtime to the KiwiAgent session that wrote it, or learn no session did. Later tasks needing hand attribution ("Being told while the work is in play", "A verification failure that is not ours") can read the same .agent/sessions/*.json registries FileHands already writes, via a new FileHands instance or by reading the files directly, rather than building attribution again.

A verification failure that is not ours [tested] (Foreign failure, Narrowed to the function, No other hand no excuse, Retry before asking, Ours on the second run, Held rather than verified, Budget spared): Verification is mechanical and runs over the files the tasks name; with a second hand in the workspace, some of what fails there was never this feature's doing.
files: src/agent/session/file-hands.ts, src/agent/session/stale-write-guard.ts, src/agent/phases/verification-attribution.ts, src/agent/phases/verification.ts, src/agent/phases/tasks-file.ts, src/chat/chat-view-provider.ts, src/extension.ts, package.json, test/verification-attribution.test.ts, test/verification.test.ts
proves: Foreign failure → test/verification-attribution.test.ts classifyFailure > foreign_failure_a_file_no_session_of_this_feature_wrote_and_another_hand_changed_since_is_foreign, Narrowed to the function → test/verification-attribution.test.ts classifyFailure > narrowed_to_the_function_a_failing_test_whose_own_function_another_hand_changed_is_foreign_even_though_this_feature_wrote_the_rest, No other hand no excuse → test/verification-attribution.test.ts classifyFailure > no_other_hand_no_excuse_nothing_changed_since_this_features_own_write_so_the_failure_is_the_features, Retry before asking → test/verification.test.ts runVerification > retry_before_asking_an_all_foreign_run_waits_and_runs_the_same_suites_again_before_being_reported, Ours on the second run → test/verification.test.ts runVerification > ours_on_the_second_run_a_failure_thats_foreign_first_but_the_features_own_on_the_retry_is_handed_to_the_implementer, Held rather than verified → test/verification.test.ts runVerification > held_rather_than_verified_an_all_foreign_run_without_a_retry_is_held_and_recorded_on_the_board_naming_the_files_and_the_hand, Budget spared → test/verification.test.ts countsAgainstBudget > budget_spared_an_all_foreign_held_outcome_does_not_count_against_the_budget
note: "Retry before asking"/"Ours on the second run"/"Held rather than verified"/"Budget spared" are proven as pure orchestration logic in runVerification/countsAgainstBudget with an injected Attribute mock, decoupled from FileHands; "Foreign failure"/"Narrowed to the function"/"No other hand no excuse" are proven against real FileHands registries in verification-attribution.test.ts, since that is where the actual file/hand/function classification lives. The user-facing "asked whether to run again, hand them to the implementer anyway, or accept them" (askAboutForeignFailures in chat-view-provider.ts) is left untested, consistent with this file's existing convention of no unit tests for its vscode UI glue (chat-view-provider.ts has no test file); the pure logic it calls (runVerification, recordVerification, handToImplementer) is otherwise fully covered.
built: FileHands.ownSnapshot(feature, path) and recordWrite(path, mtimeMs, text?) (src/agent/session/file-hands.ts) — the feature's own last-known content of a file, by mtime, across its sessions' registries. StaleWriteGuard now snapshots write content alongside mtime (src/agent/session/stale-write-guard.ts). New src/agent/phases/verification-attribution.ts: failureFiles(output, baseDir), classifyFailure(failure, hands, feature, cwd): Classification, narrowToFunction(path, currentText, ownText, line) using code-structure's readStructure for function-level diffing. src/agent/phases/verification.ts: runVerification now takes optional attribute: Attribute and retry: RetryOptions, returns VerificationOutcome { record, failures, held: HeldFailure[] }; attributeWith(hands, feature, cwd): Attribute wires classifyFailure in; countsAgainstBudget(outcome): boolean. VerificationRecord (tasks-file.ts) gained an optional foreign field naming files/hand. chat-view-provider.ts's verify() wires attribution+retry and calls askAboutForeignFailures(feature, held) on a held outcome (Run again / Hand to implementer anyway / Accept via vscode.window.showWarningMessage, untested UI glue per this codebase's convention). New kiwiAgent.verifyRetrySeconds setting (package.json), read by Verifier.retrySeconds() and wired in src/extension.ts.

What earlier tasks left:
- Being told while the work is in play [tested]: NoticeOfAnotherHand (src/agent/session/notice-of-another-hand.ts) implements SessionHooks.postToolUse: tracks, per session, the mtime it last saw of every file it read or wrote (WRITE_TOOLS ∪ Read), and on every tool call reports any tracked file whose mtime moved since — one line naming the file and (via FileHands.handFor/describeHand) who, or "Notice: N files changed since you last saw them." when several moved at once — then suppresses that file until the session sees it again (a read, or its own write, clears the flag). Added unconditionally alongside StaleWriteGuard in setupFor()'s composeHooks(...) in src/extension.ts, so every mode and both engines get it. FileHands (src/agent/session/file-hands.ts) gained handFor(path, mtimeMs): Promise<Hand | undefined>, like whoWrote but including this session's own registry, factored through a shared private find(); it's what both NoticeOfAnotherHand and the task board use to attribute a file's current mtime. Task (src/agent/phases/tasks-file.ts) gained a `foreignFiles: string[]` field (schema default [], carried through parseBoard/deriveBoard/updateTask, filtered to stay a subset of `files`); TaskProgress gained a matching optional `foreignFiles?: string[]`, replaced wholesale whenever the caller supplies it. taskBoardTools(feature, hands?: FileHands) (src/agent/openai-session/tools/task-board.ts) takes an optional FileHands now; UpdateTask, whenever `files` is given, computes foreignFiles by checking handFor on each file — no hand, or a hand whose `feature` differs from this one, is foreign — and detail() shows a `foreign changes:` line when the list is non-empty. extension.ts constructs a FileHands per session for both the new hook and for taskBoardTools's call site at ownTools. (files: src/agent/session/notice-of-another-hand.ts, src/agent/session/file-hands.ts, src/agent/phases/tasks-file.ts, src/agent/phases/legacy-tasks.ts, src/agent/openai-session/tools/task-board.ts, src/extension.ts, test/notice-of-another-hand.test.ts, test/task-board-tools.test.ts, test/task-board-fixture.ts, test/plan-step.test.ts, test/plan-view.test.ts)
